To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

automation can be classified into four types (information acquisition, information analysis, decision/action selection, and action implementation) and that automation can be characterized in terms of four levels (manual, supervisory control, procedural automation, and full automation).

automation can be categorized into four types and a range of levels and that the types and levels of an application of automation should be determined on the basis of the performance consequences of the application.

(a) automation can be applied in a variety of ways; (b) automation should be applied in ways that maximize human performance, minimize the costs of decision-action consequences, and minimize the costs of automation reliability; and (c) the types and levels of automated functions should be determined by the nature of the human-machine system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the design, evaluation, and application of human-computer systems in which the computer is an active, intelligent agent.
the development and evaluation of human-machine systems in which the human and machine are highly interdependent and interact in complex, real-time, decision making and action selection tasks.
the development and evaluation of a model for types of functions and levels of automation in human-machine systems.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
automation should be applied in a way that maximizes the benefits of automation to human performance, while at the same time minimizing the costs of automation.
the model presented is useful as a guide for designing automation in human-machine systems.
the types and levels of appropriate automation depend on the specific system and task requirements, and on the human and technical capabilities of the automation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have developed a framework for automation design that can be applied to any human-machine system, that is, any system in which a human operator interacts with a computer-based machine.
the human operator is a key element in the design of automation and should be viewed as a resource to be used and managed in the design process.
the model provides a basis for making appropriate choices about automation in terms of the human performance, reliability, and economic costs of the automation system.
The main takeaway from our work is that
automation design should be based on an understanding of the human operator's task demands and the human operator's capabilities.
the design of automation should be guided by a systematic consideration of the types of functions that are automated and the extent to which they are automated.
the design of human-machine systems requires an understanding of the nature of human performance and the nature of automation in the context of the task to be performed.
